description: The SAGE crop calendar dataset maps typical planting and harvesting dates for 19 crops worldwide, together with derived climate statistics such as the average temperature at planting, obtained by merging the calendars with CRU monthly climatologies. It was produced by the Center for Sustainability and the Global Environment (SAGE) at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and is described in Sacks and colleagues' 2010 paper in Global Ecology and Biogeography. Coverage is global, gridded at 5 arc-minutes and 0.5 degree, as a static description of crop seasons, not a time series. Files are NetCDF and ArcINFO ASCII grids, free to download; no licence is stated, and users are asked to email the dataset author when they download so that use can be tracked. Caveats: the calendars compile national and subnational sources from around 2000 and do not reflect later shifts in sowing dates, and SAGE itself points to MIRCA2000 as an alternative with similar information. For simulation it tells crop and hazard models when fields are planted or harvested, so that the timing of floods, droughts or heat waves can be converted into crop damage for exposure and climate adaptation studies. It is related to the Global Dataset of Historical Yields record in this catalogue, which gives the yields over the same seasons.
